_comment: An example pack table, using only well-known public MCP servers.
Notice the shape of the problem it solves: the `github` server bundles four
unrelated domains — code, issues, pull requests and notifications — behind a
single on/off switch. Packs let you reach into it by purpose.
`filesystem::read_file` is deliberately claimed by TWO packs (`code` and
`files`). That's the normal case: packs overlap, and turning one on must not
`disabled` is the list of tools nobody claims, WITH a reason next to each.
Write the reason in a comment in your own code; this file keeps it as prose

github.list_notifications: the client renders notifications itself; this tool just duplicates it and costs ~400 tokens per request
github.mark_notification_read: same — the client marks reads locally

packs.title: Reading code
packs.desc: Find files, search, read history — for asking questions about a repo

packs.title: Working issues
packs.desc: Read, file, close and comment on issues

packs.title: Pull requests
packs.note: Merge is destructive — some clients put this pack behind a confirmation.

packs.title: Editing files
packs.desc: Read, write, move — for actually changing things on disk

packs.title: Querying data
packs.desc: Look at tables and run read queries

packs.title: Posting to Slack
packs.desc: Send messages and upload files to your workspace
